title: people-ops
text:
people-ops

Samir (Eng Manager): Quick question — returning partially from parental leave in August; school closures mean I need a few full days off scattered in Sep/Oct. How do we handle intermittent days without burning through PTO or messing up my leave paperwork?
Ravi (IC): Yep, curious — does intermittent count as a new leave period or is it covered under the original parental leave approval?
Ava (People Ops): Hi @Samir — good timing to check. Short answer: we can approve intermittent unpaid days as an addendum to your existing leave in many cases, but we need to confirm payroll and benefits impact. Can you share the dates pattern (roughly)?
Samir (Eng Manager): Mostly school closures: Sep 9, Oct 14, and a few ad-hoc days (~3) between mid-Sept and end-Oct. I plan to be 60% back starting Aug 1 (3 days/week on-site) and then fully back Nov 1.
Ava (People Ops): Thanks. Two things for us to coordinate: 1) paperwork addendum so HR records the intermittent unpaid days linked to your parental leave window, 2) payroll coding so those days are either unpaid leave or use your PTO depending on your preference and remaining balance.
Laura (Payroll): If Samir opts to use PTO for those days we just code normal PTO. If unpaid, payroll needs an LOA code (FMLA/Parental Addendum) so benefits continuation is preserved. Important: unpaid days can affect 401k employer contributions for that pay period.
Samir (Eng Manager): Okay — prefer unpaid so PTO stays for emergencies. Do unpaid days affect my mid-year performance review or equity vesting?
Ava (People Ops): Short answer: performance reviews are manager/skip-level decisions; we have guidance to avoid penalizing people for leaves. For equity vesting, short unpaid periods can pause service for vesting if they exceed plan thresholds — I will check your plan vesting window and confirm.
PeopleOps Bot: Form received: parental-leave-addendum submitted by Samir at 2539876560 — link: https://intranet.redwood/peopleops/forms/2539876560
Ava (People Ops): Thanks @PeopleOps Bot. @Laura I created an addendum draft and attached the dates. Can payroll flag the pay periods around Sep/Oct for potential 0-hours days?
Laura (Payroll): Got it — I will reserve the LOA codes and send a short runbook for managers on how to submit timecards for 0-hour unpaid days. ETA EOD.
Ravi (IC): One more — Samir, will your on-call or manager rotation need coverage on those days?
Samir (Eng Manager): Yes, will need on-call handoff for Sep 9 and Oct 14. Planning to swap with Ravi for Sep 9 if he can. Also need to confirm whether my 60% schedule in Aug triggers a temporary manager-level coverage plan.
Ravi (IC): I can take Sep 9 on-call. For longer manager coverage, happy to coordinate with the team.
Ava (People Ops): Great. Action items: 1) Samir — confirm final dates and whether unpaid is confirmed (reply here). 2) Laura — prepare LOA codes + runbook (EOD). 3) Samir & Ravi — update on-call rota and note handoffs in the team calendar. 4) Ava — confirm equity vesting impact by tomorrow.
Samir (Eng Manager): Confirming unpaid for those days. I'll update calendar and post handoffs. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
Ava (People Ops): I'll follow up with a short confirmation email and a tiny checklist you can copy into calendar events:
```
- Add LOA addendum to employee file (People Ops)
- Mark pay periods with LOA code (Payroll)
- Manager posts handoff in calendar + notes (Manager)
- Confirm vesting impact & send summary (People Ops)
```
Ava (People Ops): Ping me if anything changes — happy to help route approvals. :heart:
